idiom_name: statically resolved overloads and extension functions on marker types; reified inline functions for type tests
implementation_notes: Kotlin's overload resolution is a compile-time process, and extension functions are resolved statically from the static type of the receiver: the spec orders candidates as members of the receiver type first, then extensions by scope, and extension calls are dispatched statically rather than virtually. A set of extensions (or overloads) on marker classes is therefore a real tag ladder - the marker class is the tag, the receiver's static type selects the implementation, and nothing is read at run time. What replaces the classic structure: extension-function overloads on tag types for closed sets, and inline functions with reified type parameters (which make the type name usable for is T / T::class checks) when the type must be inspected - that check is a runtime test and only the surrounding call is inlined. The classic form is still justified when the decision must be taken inside generic code, because a plain generic body cannot branch on T at compile time.
pitfalls: Extension functions are resolved statically, so calling one through a supertype reference silently selects the supertype's extension; there is no virtual dispatch to override it, which surprises readers who expect Java-like behaviour.

Reified type parameters require inline, and inline functions may not use non-public API of their enclosing class if they are public - a tag-mapping helper built on reified types leaks that restriction into the API surface.
when (T::class) / is T on a reified parameter is a runtime check that does not narrow T in the surrounding code, so a ladder written that way is a runtime dispatch with compile-time dressing.
sources: Kotlin language specification, Overload resolution (member callables before extensions; extensions ordered by scope; static resolution), https://kotlinlang.org/spec/overload-resolution.html
Kotlin language specification, Runtime type information (reified type parameters; runtime-available types), https://kotlinlang.org/spec/runtime-type-information.html
